situation: Author was placed in a role by a recruiter and believed it was temporary.
choice: Quit the job after 97 days, just past the 90-day retention threshold.
outcome: The company paid a large referral fee to the recruiter, causing the author distress.
main_reason: Author felt horrible about the company paying a fee due to their timing.
advice: Be honest and open about intentions to avoid wasting recruiters' time.
quote: I felt HORRIBLE when I found out the company had paid a referral fee of several thousand dollars to the recruiter. 7 days past the 90 day cutoff.
author: Keith

situation: Author changed careers from IT to a different field eight years ago.
choice: The author switched from an IT career to a completely different field.
outcome: The author lost their job in the new field and returned to IT temporarily.
main_reason: The author determined the previous line of work was not for them.
advice: Be honest in interviews about career gaps and emphasize applicable skills on the resume.
author: Keith

situation: Mechanical engineer worked in test engineering and construction, then discovered programming through automation tasks.
choice: Switched careers from engineering to programming after taking CS classes and attending a career fair.
outcome: Loved the initial transition but now struggles with poor documentation and legacy code in a corporate role.
main_reason: Developed a strong interest in programming while automating repetitive engineering tasks.
advice: First job does not define career; pursue interests and seek opportunities to switch if desired.
quote: Fast forward two years and I'm trying to hang on to that passion as hard as I can, because my job is sucking it all away.
author: yankees13
